verdict.rationale: Cloudflare documents that its TURN service uses Anycast, so a client connecting to turn.cloudflare.com automatically reaches the closest Cloudflare location, and WebRTC traffic is relayed through Cloudflare's network. That evidence covers only the TURN relay path. Nothing shows how SFU media is routed to a nearby point of presence, and there is no published list of regions or locations. Missing for 10: documentation of SFU media ingress at the nearest edge location, a documented region/PoP list or map of the media-carrying network, independent latency corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, clients connect to a nearby point of presence and the vendor documents the regions or edge network that carries media

citations.quote: When a client tries to connect to `turn.cloudflare.com`, it _automatically_ connects to the Cloudflare location closest to them.
Cloudflare TURN uses [Anycast ↗︎](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/cdn/glossary/anycast-network/), so you do not have to deploy regional TURN servers or load balancers.
Relay WebRTC traffic through Cloudflare when a NAT or firewall prevents a direct connection.
